newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Austria says no more tax hikes in 1998-99.
newsitem.headline: Austria says no more tax hikes in 1998-99.

text.p: Austrian Finance Minister Rudolf Edlinger said in a television interview late on Friday that taxes would not be increased and that the government would not implement any further austerity measures in the next two years.

He reiterated earlier statements that Austria's budget deficit for this year was estimated at 68 billion schillings ($5.5 billion), well in line with the Maastricht criteria for the starting group of European Economic and Monetary Union (EMU) in 1999.
Edlinger said he was convinced that budget deficit level could also be maintained in 1998 and 1999.
However, he said it was vital to keep an extremely tight rein on spending and that some "adjustments on the revenue side" would be necessary.
Edlinger said there would be no need to revise the current tax model before the year 2,000.

He is due to submit the 1998 and 1999 budgets to the council of ministers on July 22 this year. Last week he said the federal budget deficit in 1998 would come in between 2.6 and 2.7 percent of gross domestic product (GDP).
